Which tells me that you either didn't play it very much, or that you have low expectations and/or standards. There is practically no emergent gameplay whatsoever, because the galaxy is simply too big. You'll rarely run into other players, so they might as well not even exist. Everything this game has to offer was programmed/scripted by the developers. The result is that the Elite experience is pretty much defined by repetition.

  • Missions: Lackluster. There's only like a handful of different mission types and you have to be lucky for an interesting one to even show up. Besides that there are the ridiculous skill-requirements where the only missions that are worth it financially, require you to have extremely high combat or trade ranks. I played for almost 300 hours and I still haven't reached the combat rank 'Elite' (close to becoming deadly though). Missions, in their current form, are half-assed.
  • Bounty Hunting (PVE): The very definition of a grind and on top of that poorly implemented. Why it's a grind is obvious: You shoot down hordes of ships to earn money, so you can buy equipment and ships to shoot down ships with. The poor implementation is how the ship spawns in a RES are not random. Whenever a player jumps into an RES, the game creates a new instance of it. There are three types of instances: Big, small and mixed pirate spawns. This means that if you jump into a RES and are greeted by a pirate Adder, you can exit to the main menu, go into the game again and hope that you get a big-ship-only instance this time. If you don't, you'll be stuck fighting cannon-fodder that will neither give you any money, nor be fun to fight. It's just a complete waste of time once you fly a bigger ship. Sometimes you have to go back to the main menu dozens of times. Fun, fun, fun...
  • Exploration: Exploration, also known as "I haven't heard of SpaceEngine yet". As little gameplay as SE has at the moment, it still blows ED out of the water in this aspect mainly because it actually gives you stuff to do. Exploration in ED is just jumping and scanning...forever.
  • Trading: It's similar to exploration in that there is barely any gameplay there, as it boils down to jump, dock, jump, dock, jump, dock,... . It's also similar to bounty hunting, because the only benefit from doing it is gaining money so you can do it more.
  • Piracy (PVE): Similar to missions it's only something you do to mix things up in between endless repetition. It's just not worth it. You have to find a trader, possibly interdict him, get his cargo, pick it up and then find a black market to sell it in, only to find out that you barely made any money.
  • Piracy (PVP): 1: Good luck finding anyone. 2: Have fun with combat-loggers.

tl;dr: Elite, by any stretch of the imagination, is no great game. It's a fairly decent, but not great. It's clear that Frontier bit off more than they can chew. ED has potential - tons of it - but that's about it. There's no way you're ever going to fly a decently kitted Anaconda without going through insane amounts of busywork.

When a train spills all of its spaghetti

What the hell am I looking at?

Are those steam pipes?

Those are actually flues from the fire box directly to the smoke stack. Normally they are surrounded by water which is heated by the hot gases escaping through these flues. The water is heated, turns into steam, and is collected via a steam dome at the top of the boiler and redirected to the cylinders to power the locomotive. There are a TON of these flues to increase the surface area by which you are imparting heat from the flues to the water.

There are, of course, a few problems to worry about with these 'fire tube' boilers. Too high of a pressure is bad and could lead to a blow out like what we see here. If you have too much water in the boiler some could end up being drawn up with the generated steam, fouling the works (water in the cylinders is obviously bad for the engine). Too little water and you might end up uncovering the top of the firebox, heating it hotter than it can withstand (if the firebox fails, steam could be exhausted through the firebox into the cabin of the locomotive with fatal consequences). A little too hot under the collar...
